text:
ajay: Heads-up — after yesterday's routing patch (multi-variant compat fallback change) we're seeing worse tail latency on the small-req path. Suspect batching fragmentation. Anyone else?

maya: Saw the alert. noise on p95 for text-gen routes went up ~18% during peak. Repro with loadgen?

ajay: Yes ran a short replay against staging. Profiling shows avg batch_size down from ~6 to ~2 for some routes when compat sets include the fallback variants.

sophie: That matches my local trace: when router annotates compat_set=[m1,q8,m1-compat] it tries to coalesce, but fallback injection forces immediate flush to preserve token_budget. Result: many 1-item batches.

rhys: Token budget policy change we shipped reduced per-request token_budget from 128->96 for tier B. Combined with stricter max_wait ms it hurts assembly.

ajay: Key logs from staging run: 
```
[batcher] formed_batch size=1 reason=compat_mismatch reqs=1 token_budget=96 wait=12ms
[batcher] formed_batch size=5 reason=max_wait reqs=5 token_budget=96 wait=50ms
```
Shows compat_mismatch causing premature flushes.

maya: Can we confirm whether kernel selection changes (different model variants choose different kernels) make the runtime mark variants as incompatible? I remember compat is a fairly conservative check.

sophie: Right — current compat rule compares (arch, dtype, kernel_hint). Kernel_hint differs when quant profiles differ (q8 vs q4). Even if kernels could run in same queue, compat treats them as distinct. That triggers separate batch formation buckets.

rhys: Two quick options: 1) relax compat check to allow grouping if kernels are 'compatible at runtime' (measured via a cheap probe), or 2) adjust token_budget/queue_policy to favor waiting a bit longer when batcher sees fragmentation.

ajay: I prototyped (2) on staging: bump per-route token_budget_target by +32 for model-family with many variants and set max_wait 20ms -> batch size recovered to ~5 and p95 improved. But cost went up ~7%.

maya: Tradeoff seems expected. We should aim for dynamic token_budget: keep strict for single-variant traffic, relax when fragmentation detected. Could be heuristic: if >20% batches size<=2 for 30s, increase budget by 25%.

sophie: Also propose a soft-compat grouping: tag variants as "compat-soft" if kernels differ only in dtype/quant but share same launch path. Batcher can tentatively group them but include variant-level metadata to later reroute if kernel fails. Safer than full relax.

rhys: Perf-bot ran microbenchmarks: grouping soft-compat reduces average latency 12% and increases throughput 18% on our 8G profile. But worst-case cpu for kernel selection increases slightly.

perf-bot: Benchmark summary (short):
- baseline (strict compat): mean latency 45ms, p95 120ms, avg batch 2.1
- token_budget+32: mean 49ms, p95 95ms, avg batch 4.9
- soft-compat: mean 43ms, p95 88ms, avg batch 5.1

ajay: Solid. Next steps: Sophie will prototype soft-compat grouping in batcher, Rhys will add adaptive token_budget heuristic, Maya will run an A/B in staging with realistic multi-variant traffic.

sophie: I'll open a small PR to batcher that adds "soft_compat" tag and a fallback path if a kernel mismatch is discovered at execution time. Will include unit tests and a metric for "soft_compat_fallback_count".

rhys: I'll add the adaptive token_budget feature behind a feature-flag and a per-route config: {min_budget, max_budget, trigger_threshold}. Default disabled.

maya: I'll prepare the staging experiment and include traces + the batch_size histogram. Let's keep a close eye on cost delta.

ajay: Great. If we converge on soft-compat + adaptive budget we can get p95 back without regressing cost too much. Tagging @sre for rollout window. :thumbsup:
